message.subject: Re: Stage38 review: close stale host/test/rule references before push
message.body:
Three corrections accepted, follow-up reviewed, and a bounded acceptance verdict below. No blockers. Still source-only and read-only; nothing in /tmp/enola-hash-read-diagnostic/ or the worktree was modified.

1. RULE REFERENCE - MY ERROR, CORRECTED. The pinned governing text is final/PROMOTION_RULE.md, 17 lines, sha256 56f86609eee796c6675fec459a3edab91fa0da888406a0a937a1a8912c34e736, which is what cli-pairs/pins.json records and what I re-verified by hashing. 6724a0d8 is the earlier 13-line archived copy and my report cited it; please read that reference as corrected. I diffed the two rather than take the claim: the 17-line file is the 13-line text verbatim plus two appended paragraphs - the source-integration update naming source 1af548c, clean build cb6a69f and binary e9e48eb0 as superseding the overlay-only status, and the pre-timing prerequisite checkpoint naming the requested window and the ACK state. Both are status and provenance only and both restate that thresholds are unchanged. Every numeric gate I checked - primary at most 0.97, six paired wins, at most 2 percent non-primary time, at most 5 percent RSS, mean ratio below 1, sum nonincreasing, plus the retained pressure, swap and power gates - is identical in the two texts, so all six gate verdicts and their margins transfer unchanged. Timing supports the pre-timing claim: the final rule's mtime is 18:19:02 UTC, before pins frozen_at 18:26:25 UTC and before the first arm at 18:26:50 UTC, and it is one of the 26 of 26 file pins that verify.

2. HOST AUDIT - MY ERROR, WITHDRAWN. It was not absent. final/host-audit.json, primary-audit.json host_context and the per-arm host-load samples are present, and my statement that the foreign-load-disclosure clause was unsatisfied is withdrawn; it is satisfied. What I now verify and disclose:

Coverage: 30 or 31 samples per arm across all twelve, zero sampler errors, maximum sample gap 2.141 to 2.190 s, owner-PID descendants excluded, arguments omitted.

Asymmetry, stated as a direction and not netted out: per-arm mean foreign CPU runs 84.710 to 101.403 percent. Group means are baseline 92.706 against candidate 90.287, a 2.420 pp gap favouring the candidate. Per-pair candidate-minus-baseline deltas are -0.563, -1.297, -9.632, +0.723, -6.970, +3.220 pp, so the candidate ran quieter in four of six pairs - your figure confirmed.

The bound that matters, and the reason I do not think the asymmetry manufactures the result: in the two pairs where the candidate ran NOISIER, pair 4 at +0.723 pp and pair 6 at +3.220 pp, the candidate still won by 6.1843 and 6.8190 percent. And the ordering does not track load - pair 3 has the largest quiet advantage at -9.632 pp but only the second-best win, while pair 1 at -0.563 pp produced the cohort's best -7.3878 percent. Spearman rho between load delta and no-op ratio is +0.60 on six points, which is descriptive only. I am applying no causal correction, making no significance claim, and asserting no clean host: the accepted statement is a bounded shared-host engineering comparison in which the primary gain survives in the adverse-load pairs.

Composition: twenty foreign executables listed. The steady contributors are WindowServer at 28.58 to 29.12 mean, a Virtualization VM at 9.67 to 9.89, Orca at 6.58 to 7.01, a Google helper at 3.26 to 4.13 and grok at 2.84 to 2.85, none differing between arms by as much as 1 pp; the remainder are Telegram, WhatsApp, ClearVPN, codex, cliproxyapi, launchd, sysmond, triald, geod, PerfPowerServices, Activity, a decoder XPC service, a wallpaper extension and cpa-manager-plus.

My own disclosure, which the audit surfaces and I should state rather than let you find: a claude executable appears in the foreign list at 8.92 percent mean during candidate-1 against 1.53 to 3.44 percent in the other ten arms where it is listed. I sent msg_8b639025c4ba at 18:28:59 UTC, inside candidate-1's interval, so that peak is plausibly my own acknowledgement traffic. Two honest limits. The sampler records executable names without pids or arguments, and your coordinator session is also a claude process, so these receipts cannot attribute the peak to my session rather than yours and I will not claim which it was. And the direction is adverse to the candidate: load inside a candidate arm can only slow the candidate, yet pair 1 produced the largest win. So this is a disclosure, not a correction to any number.

Independent agreement on a second file: primary-audit.json's ratios reproduce my own computation exactly - initial 0.9884459385765023, no-op 0.93173615524634, body 0.9617767531390862, structural 0.9661962968071504, and RSS 0.9842946690796601, 1.0109992667155523, 1.0429326905108944, 0.9747995418098511. Its initial paired ratio 1.0256419720115437 is the positive pair I flagged.

3. FOLLOW-UP c3c481e REVIEWED, AND IT CLOSES MY TEST GAP. Verified rather than accepted:

The timed runtime is untouched. After stripping comments, buffered_hash.go and engine.go at c3c481e are code-identical to their parent, and both files at that parent are byte-identical to timed 1af548c. So the follow-up is comments plus one new test file, and the frozen binary's source is unaffected.

The guard is stronger than what I suggested and it is deterministic. I proposed recording a maximum read length; the test instead asserts on every Read that the slice IS the supplied scratch - both len(p) and the address of element zero - and fails outright if WriteTo is ever called. That pins buffer use by identity rather than by a bound, with no AllocsPerRun-style flakiness.

It demonstrably detects the intended regression rather than passing vacuously. buffered_hash_mutant.go differs from the real file in exactly one line, the WriterTo-hiding wrapper removed, and the overlay run fails precisely at buffered_hash_buffer_test.go:27 with the WriterTo message in 0.691 s, against the passing 0.751 s. That is the discriminating evidence I could not produce from source alone.

Scope of the new guard, so the archive does not overstate it: it pins that the supplied scratch is used and that WriterTo is not taken. It does not pin the 64 KiB size or the four-worker count, so a later change to either still passes. That is the right scope for the mechanism, but the memory bound's magnitude remains policy documented by comment only.

One non-blocking safety note: t.Fatal from the reader is sound here only because readHash runs on the test goroutine. If that reader is ever reused inside boundedFileHashes's workers, Fatal from a non-test goroutine would end that goroutine without failing the test properly. Worth one comment line if anyone reuses the type.

The comment edits adopt all four hardening notes from my source review - scratch must be nonempty, each caller owns its scratch and digest, the returned digest does not alias scratch because EncodeToString copies before the next read, and the bound is per invocation and not process-wide - plus the empty-digest sentinel rationale. And the engine.go comment now preserves the recorded contention rationale while stating that buffer reuse alone does not disprove it and that Product measurements cover the bounded candidate only. That resolves my principal caveat exactly as I would have written it.

Hygiene, small: followup-tests.log records only the ok line and 0.751 s, with no command line, no -run pattern and no -count=1, so the log by itself cannot show which tests ran or that caching was bypassed. The elapsed time is consistent with real execution and the mutation log does name the specific failure. Adding the command line would make the receipt self-contained; same class as the earlier full-suite receipt note, and I am not asking for a rerun.

4. WHAT STANDS FROM MY EARLIER REPORT, UNCHANGED. All six performance gates PASS with the margins as sent: primary 0.931736155 against 0.97, 76.77 ms and 3.826 pp of headroom, and leave-one-pair-out keeps every variant under 0.97; six paired wins from -6.1843 to -7.3878 percent; non-primary times all improvements at -1.155406, -3.822325, -3.380370; RSS -1.570533, +1.099927, +4.293269, -2.520046; mean ratio 0.9620387859422697; sum -552.90 ms at -2.606542502492 percent with every term negative. Order AB BA AB BA AB BA, twelve arms, all exit 0, inside the window and after not_before_utc. Pressure 3519 samples all level 1, worst gap 0.2755 s, full bracketing; zero new Swapouts; 24 of 24 power observations AC with lowpowermode 0 and charge 41 to 33 percent above the floor; per-sample wall-minus-monotonic spread 0.242 to 1.185 ms so no suspension. 84 of 84 exits, one graph hash per label matching Stage37's 194f7fbf and 777ca168, 36 of 36 incremental equals cold, twelve silent no-ops, 72 of 72 broker successes, payload deltas +3084, +3, +4 fully explained by run-identifier length. Three binary and 26 file pins verify; argv differs only by --repeat with no ENOLA_GRAPH_PROFILE.

The two findings I would still put in the archive are unchanged. Body RSS +4.293269 percent, +35.898 MiB, is the tightest gate in the cohort and 256 KiB of added scratch is two orders of magnitude short of explaining it; I offer no attribution, only the note that a larger body workload could approach 5 percent on an unidentified mechanism. And the initial scenario has overlapping ranges with one positive pair at +2.5642 percent, so its -1.155 percent median clears a regression bound but is not an established improvement. summary_scans and derived_indexes remain nondeterministic and I did not normalize them away. The duplicate control pin is labeling only. The charge caveat is scheduling only and is not a revival of the throttle inference I withdrew.

5. VERDICT. Bounded acceptance, no blockers. The frozen gates in the pinned 56f86609 rule are met on the receipts in this tree; correctness, provenance, pressure, swap, power and host disclosure prerequisites are satisfied; the one test gap from my source review is closed by c3c481e, which leaves the timed runtime untouched. Scope of what that supports: a limited engineering promotion on one host, one Product tree, six pairs, with a disclosed 2.42 pp foreign-load asymmetry favouring the candidate and the gain surviving in the adverse-load pairs. It is not statistical significance, not a clean host, not resident-watch latency, not near-zero fresh no-op completion, not complete current-main historical coverage, and not a general claim for other repositories or storage devices. Absolute seconds stay inside this cohort.

Retaining source-only availability; no worker_done. Standing offer continues for any future cohort.
